ScheduleIterAlg.note: ValidParameters.py:349 lists [0,1,2,3,4]. Value 4 is remapped to _ScheduleIterAlg=0 (Solution.py:599). Using [0,1,2,3] covers both sides: 1 makes scheduleIterAlg==1 True; 0/2/3 make it False.

KernelLanguage.note: ValidParameters.py:915 - only valid value is Assembly. No variation possible.

self.states.overflowedResources.note: StateValues.overflowedResources (KernelWriter.py:183) is an int initialized to 0. All write-paths assign one of {0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8}: 1=too many vgprs, 2=too many sgprs, 3=half-store batch, 4=occupancy limit, 5=LDS scheduling conflict, 6=SIA2 occupancy, 7=invalid LSU code, 8=LDS space. The branch predicate is a truth-test (nonzero == True). Domain {0,1} is the minimal pair that exercises both sides.

u.note: Loop index ranging 0..LoopIters-1 (KernelWriter.py:3064-3065). Domain [0,1,2,3] exercises u==0 (ForceUnrollSubIter true-arm), u in interior, and u at or beyond threshold for doReadB false-arm.

iui.note: Inner-unroll index 0..InnerUnroll-1 (KernelWriter.py:4055). The gate iui*numReadsIterCoalescedB < InnerUnroll is false only when iui >= InnerUnroll/numReadsIterCoalescedB. iui=0 always satisfies the gate; iui=1 can violate it when numReadsIterCoalescedB>=InnerUnroll.

kernel['LoopIters'].note: Derived: LoopUnroll = DepthU/LocalSplitU/InnerUnroll; LoopIters = LoopUnroll/MatrixInstK (MI path) or LoopUnroll/(NumDotElements*NumWaveSplitK) (dot path). Typical values 1-16 powers-of-2. Drives threshold in normal-path doReadB comparison.

kernel['PrefetchLocalRead'].note: YAML scalar int 0..128 (ValidParameters.py:284). numItersPLR = PLR%(LoopIters//WLR) or PLR%LoopIters. PLR=0 gives numItersPLR=0 (no prefetch, doReadB threshold = full LoopIters/numIterPerCoalescedReadB); PLR=1 gives numItersPLR=1 (common case); PLR=2 exercises double-buffer. Covers both sides of the doReadB < threshold comparison.

kernel['InnerUnroll'].note: YAML int, ValidParameters.py:906: [1,2,4,8,16,32,64]. Drives numIterPerCoalescedReadB = max(1, numReadsIterCoalescedB//InnerUnroll) and the inner-unroll gate iui*numReadsIterCoalescedB < InnerUnroll. Values 1,2,4 cover the common range and exercise both sides of the gate.

kernel['PrefetchGlobalRead'].note: YAML int 0..16 (ValidParameters.py:282). hasLiveLdsData = kernel['PrefetchGlobalRead']. PGR=0 disables next-loop OR branch; PGR=1 enables it (common); PGR=2 double-buffer variant. Domain [0,1,2] covers both sides of the hasLiveLdsData branch.

kernel['ForceUnrollSubIter'].note: Derived bool (Solution.py:2034-2037): True only when EnableMatrixInstruction and not ExpandPointerSwap and DepthU==MatrixInstK and PGR>0 and not 1LDSBuffer and MIWaveTile[0]>2 and MIWaveTile[1]>2 and even MIWaveTile etc. Both bool values needed: ForceUnrollSubIter=True forces doReadB=1 if u==0 else 0; False takes normal comparison path.

kernel['EnableMatrixInstruction'].note: YAML bool (ValidParameters.py:1054). Selects numReadsIterCoalescedB path: MI path uses ceil(lrvwUnrollB/MIInputPerThreadB); non-MI path uses lrvwUnrollB//NumDotElements if UseDotInstruction else 1. Both values needed to cover both code branches.

kernel['LocalReadVectorWidthB'].note: YAML int [-1,1,2,4,8,16,32] (ValidParameters.py:821). -1 resolved at setup; effective value drives lrvwUnrollB when UnrollMajorLDSB=True: lrvwUnrollB = LRVWB. Values {1,4,8} give numReadsIterCoalescedB = {1,1..2,2..4} covering both sides of the inner-unroll gate when combined with InnerUnroll.

kernel['LocalReadVectorWidthA'].note: YAML int [-1,1,2,4,8,16,32] (ValidParameters.py:820). Used when EnableMatrixInstruction: WLR = max(LRVWA//MIInputPerThread, 1); numItersPLR = PLR%(LoopIters//WLR). Values {1,4,8} vary WLR and thus numItersPLR boundary.

kernel['UnrollMajorLDSB'].note: Derived bool (KernelWriter.py:6427-6430). True: lrvwUnrollB = LocalReadVectorWidthB; False: lrvwUnrollB = 1. Switching this toggles the effective coalescing width for B reads and changes numReadsIterCoalescedB.

kernel['MatrixInstruction'].note: YAML list [M,N,K,B,...] (ValidParameters.py:687=-1 means unconstrained). Drives MatrixInstK=mi[2], MIInputPerThreadB=N*K*B//WavefrontSize. Four representative configs: [32,32,2,1] gives MatrixInstK=2,MIInputPerThreadB=1; [16,16,16,1] gives K=16,miB=4; [32,32,8,1] gives K=8,miB=4; [16,16,32,1] gives K=32,miB=8.

kernel['DepthU'].note: YAML int 2..1024 (ValidParameters.py:862). LoopUnroll = DepthU/LocalSplitU/InnerUnroll. Powers of 2 in {8,16,32,64} are most common in production kernels and exercise ForceUnrollSubIter condition (DepthU==MatrixInstK when DepthU small).

kernel['LocalSplitU'].note: Derived: WorkGroup[2] in MI path, 1 if WaveSplitK in non-MI path (Solution.py:633,661). Divides DepthU to give LoopUnroll. Values {1,2,4} cover common production configs.

kernel['NumDotElements'].note: Derived int, default 2 (Solution.py:689). Used in non-MI UseDotInstruction path: numReadsIterCoalescedB = lrvwUnrollB//NumDotElements. Only value 2 observed in practice.

kernel['UseDotInstruction'].note: Bool derived from ISA/dtype capabilities. Selects non-MI coalesced-read path when True. Both sides needed: UseDotInstruction=False gives numReadsIterCoalescedB=1; True gives numReadsIterCoalescedB=lrvwUnrollB//NumDotElements.

kernel['NumWaveSplitK'].note: In MI path always 1 (Solution.py:634); in non-MI path = WorkGroup[2] when WaveSplitK. Used in LoopIters = LoopUnroll/(NumDotElements*NumWaveSplitK). Values {1,2} cover both paths.

kernel['MIInputPerThread'].note: Derived from MatrixInstruction: MIInputPerThread = N*K*B//WavefrontSize (where N=mi[1],K=mi[2],B=mi[3],WFS=64). Common values: 1 (f32 MFMA), 2 (bf16 32x32x4), 4 (f16/bf16 larger K), 8 (f8 kernels). Used in WLR factor for numItersPLR boundary.

kernel['MIInputPerThreadB'].note: Same derivation as MIInputPerThread for symmetric data types (Solution.py:651-652). Used directly in numReadsIterCoalescedB = ceil(lrvwUnrollB/MIInputPerThreadB). Values {1,2,4,8} match MFMA instruction families.

kernel['HalfPLR'].note: YAML int [0,1,2,3] (ValidParameters.py:1048). Not directly in the doReadB predicate but guards half-PLR split code after doReadB. Values {0,1} cover enabled/disabled.

kernel['UseCustomMainLoopSchedule'].note: YAML int [-1,0,1] (ValidParameters.py:974). Affects uNext computation path (doFullPackCodePrefetch), which influences doNext and thus the next-loop OR-arm. All 3 values cover the scheduler paths.

kernel['MIWaveTile'].note: YAML list of two ints. Both elements must be >2 and even for ForceUnrollSubIter to be enabled. Values [2,2] disables ForceUnrollSubIter; [4,2] partially meets criteria; [4,4] enables it fully. Used to exercise both branches of ForceUnrollSubIter.

kernel['1LDSBuffer'].note: YAML int 0 or 1 (Solution.py:1127: default 0). Drives ForceUnrollSubIter guard (requires not 1LDSBuffer). Both values needed to cover that branch.

kernel['ExpandPointerSwap'].note: Derived bool (Solution.py:1126,1994-2005). ForceUnrollSubIter requires not ExpandPointerSwap. Both values needed to cover the ForceUnrollSubIter guard.

ISA asmCaps HasMFMA.note: GPU probe: True for gfx9 (gfx908/gfx90a/gfx942) and gfx950, False for gfx11/gfx12 WMMA-only. Drives MIInputPerThread computation path and EnableMatrixInstruction. Both values needed for architecture coverage.

ISA asmCaps HasWMMA.note: GPU probe: True for gfx11/gfx12/gfx1250, False for gfx9. Selects WMMA path for MIInputPerThreadB derivation. Both values needed for architecture coverage.

hasLiveLdsData.note: Derived: hasLiveLdsData = kernel['PrefetchGlobalRead'] (KernelWriter.py:4024). Boolean coercion: 0 gives False, any positive int gives True. Both values exercise the next-loop OR-arm of doReadB.

doNext.note: Derived bool: uNext > localWriteEndIter (KernelWriter.py:4040), where localWriteEndIter = LoopIters - numItersPLR - 1. True for the last few iterations when next-loop prefetch is needed. Both values exercise the next-loop OR-arm.

SuppressNoLoadLoop.note: ValidParameters.py:323 lists [False, True]; default False (GlobalParameters.py:445). Primary YAML input for the predicate when HalfPLR==0 and TailloopInNll is not effective. Subject to validity suppression at Solution.py:1845-1847.

HalfPLR.note: ValidParameters.py:1048 lists [0,1,2,3]; default 0 (GlobalParameters.py:560). 0 = no override. Any non-zero value unconditionally sets SuppressNoLoadLoop=True (Solution.py:2281-2283). Values 1,2,3 are equivalent for this predicate; domain [0,1] suffices to exercise both sides.

TailloopInNll.note: ValidParameters.py:990 lists [False, True]; default False (GlobalParameters.py:535). When True and its own validity constraints pass (Solution.py:3850-3869), unconditionally sets SuppressNoLoadLoop=False — the final override dominating all prior assignments.

BufferLoad.note: ValidParameters.py:388 lists [False, True]; default True (GlobalParameters.py:454). Required True for bufferLoad=True (Solution.py:1828). If False, bufferLoad=False, which causes the validity gate (Solution.py:1846) to force SuppressNoLoadLoop=False when yaml value is True.

KernelLanguage.note: ValidParameters.py:915 - only valid value is 'Assembly'. No variation possible; always contributes True to bufferLoad computation.

PrefetchGlobalRead.note: ValidParameters.py:282 lists [0,1,2,...,16]; default 1 (GlobalParameters.py:442). Validity gate at Solution.py:1846 requires PGR==1 for SuppressNoLoadLoop to remain True. Domain [0,1] covers the gate: 1=pass, 0=fail.

GlobalSplitU.note: ValidParameters.py:315 lists range(-1,1024+1); default 1 (GlobalParameters.py:475). Validity gate at Solution.py:1846 requires GSU==1 OR GSU==-1. Domain [-1,1,2]: -1 and 1 exercise the True-gate path; 2 exercises the False-gate path.

tc.note: tP['tensorChar'] is the literal string cM assigned in KernelWriter._initKernel via getTensorParameters: 'A' for tensorParametersA, 'B' for tensorParametersB. These are the only two call-site values.

kernel[DirectToLdsA].note: True when DirectToLds==1 or DirectToLds==2 (Solution.py:722). False when DirectToLds==0 or DirectToLds==3. May be forced False by isDirectToLdsDoable() rejection or BufferLoad=False.

kernel[DirectToLdsB].note: True when DirectToLds==1 or DirectToLds==3 (Solution.py:723). False when DirectToLds==0 or DirectToLds==2. Same conditional reset logic as DirectToLdsA.

DirectToLds.note: YAML/MsgPack solution parameter. 0=no DTL (default, GlobalParameters.py:461), 1=both A+B, 2=A only, 3=B only. Drives DirectToLdsA and DirectToLdsB derivations.

kernel[ISA].note: ISA triple (major, minor, patch). cpp SgprPreloadPad expression: checkInList(isa,{9,5,0}) || checkInList(isa,{9,0,10}) || (isa[0]==9 && isa[1]==4). True: (9,5,0)=gfx950, (9,4,2)=gfx942, (9,0,10)=gfx90a. False: (11,0,0)=gfx1100. Four values cover True on three distinct sub-conditions and False on one non-gfx9 arch. Note: Tensile gfx908->(9,0,8) which is False; gfx90a->(9,0,10) which is True.

kernel[PreloadKernArgs].note: YAML solution parameter, default True. Controls outer guard numSgprPreload > 0 (line 2266). Must be True for the predicate at line 2267 to be evaluated. Both sides needed: True to exercise the predicate, False to verify the outer guard prevents entry.

self.states.archCaps[SgprPreloadPad].note: Derived int-as-bool from kernel[ISA] via rocisa initArchCaps(). Value 1 for (9,5,0), (9,0,10), (9,4,*); value 0 for all other ISAs including gfx11xx, gfx12xx, gfx906, gfx908. Python truthiness: nonzero = True, zero = False.

self.do[\"PreLoop\"].note: Always True at runtime (compile-time constant). False is unreachable — listed only to mark the dead branch.
